preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(t, int) and 1 <= t <= 100 for t in [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit()])
preconditions.description: The first line of stdin is a single integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 100) representing the number of test cases.
Each test case consists of exactly two lines: the first line is n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100), and the second line contains n integers a₁, a₂, ..., aₙ (0 ≤ aᵢ ≤ 10⁹).

preconditions.expression: all(len(a) == n for n, a in [(int(stdin.splitlines()[i*2]), [int(x) for x in stdin.splitlines()[i*2+1].split()]) for i in range(t)])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line contains exactly n integers, where n is the value from the first line of the test case.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly one integer per test case, in the same order as the input.
Each output line is a valid integer representing the minimal possible maximum value in the sequence after any number of operations.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(stdout.splitlines()[i]) <= max(a) for i, a in enumerate([[int(x) for x in stdin.splitlines()[j*2+1].split()] for j in range(t)]))
postconditions.description: The output integer for each test case is between 0 and the maximum value in the original sequence.

postconditions.expression: all(min_possible_max(a) == int(stdout.splitlines()[i]) for i, a in enumerate([[int(x) for x in stdin.splitlines()[j*2+1].split()] for j in range(t)]))
postconditions.description: The output integer for each test case is the minimal possible maximum value achievable in the sequence after any number of operations, where min_possible_max(a) is defined as the smallest possible maximum value in any sequence derivable from a by applying the described bitwise AND operations any number of times.
